summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with metastatic cholangiocarcinoma and a history of recurrent cholangitis due to multidrug-resistant E. coli, was admitted with fevers and decreased output from his percutaneous transhepatic biliary drain (PTBD) following an iron infusion. Blood cultures confirmed MDR E. coli bacteremia, and imaging showed stable liver microabscesses with a clogged PTBD. He underwent PTBD exchange with upsizing of the catheter to improve drainage. Initial treatment with ceftazidime-avibactam, metronidazole, and planned tobramycin and tigecycline was adjusted when cultures showed sensitivity to meropenem; he was transitioned to meropenem and tigecycline, later changed to ertapenem for outpatient administration. A new PICC line was placed for IV antibiotics. He had a brief episode of bloody PTBD output after straining, which resolved spontaneously. He tolerated a PTBD capping trial and was discharged home with capped drain, on IV ertapenem and tigecycline, with plans for weekly labs, follow-up MRI, and infectious disease evaluation to determine treatment duration.
